contact_needs.B: I need people to reach out

favorite_premium.A: Pay for the one I love

opening.prompt: Who's your closest person right now?

cards.prompt: 11:48pm. You're finally drifting off. Your best friend texts: "are you up? I need to talk."

options.t: Sit straight up and call. Sleep is canceled.
Call, but warn them I'm fading fast.
Pretend I'm asleep. Text them first thing at 7am.
"Barely conscious. Tomorrow, first thing, I promise."

cards.prompt: Your closest friend hasn't texted in three weeks. Their last message was "lol".

options.t: Nothing. We go months. We're fine.
Send a meme. Low pressure, just a ping.
Check their stories. They posted three times. Hmm.
Reread "lol" four times looking for hidden meaning.

cards.prompt: A limited banner drops tonight. Your favorite character, 48 hours only. You have $30 of fun money this month.

options.t: Pull. All of it. Tonight.
Pull $10, then walk away. Probably.
Wait for the rerun. They always come back.
Skip it. That $30 already has a job.

cards.prompt: Your friend plays you a song they wrote. It's not good. They look so hopeful.

options.t: "The chorus needs work. Want notes?"
"Love the vibe. The second verse drags a bit."
"Catchy!" Notes can wait for version two.
"This is a hit." Start humming it on the spot.

cards.prompt: You and your closest person win a free week in a cabin. One bathroom. No wifi.

options.t: Perfect. Seven days of us and board games.
Love it, but I'm taking a solo walk daily.
Great. I'm driving up separately, though.
Could we make it a long weekend instead?

cards.prompt: You find $200 in a jacket you haven't worn since last winter.

options.t: Concert tickets. Tonight if possible.
Half on something fun, half saved.
Saved it, minus one iced coffee.
Savings. Future me says thanks.
It went to a bill. Romance is dead.

cards.prompt: 1am. Your friend has carried the team all night and types "one more match?" You're up at 9.

options.t: Obviously. It's never actually one more.
One more, then I'm logging off. For real.
Go "afk" and quietly never come back.
"I'm done, gg. Same time tomorrow?"

cards.prompt: Weekend trip with two friends. One just landed a job paying double yours. The rental bill hits the group chat.

options.t: Three-way split. Math is math.
Three-way split, and I'm quietly doing math.
Suggest the new salary covers a bit more.
They offered to pay more. I said yes, gratefully.

cards.prompt: Your headphones die. The ones you love are $300. The fine ones are $80.

options.t: The $300 ones. My ears deserve this.
The $300 ones, after a week of "should I?"
The $80 ones. I'll visit the nice ones online.
The $80 ones. Sound is sound.

cards.prompt: In the group chat, your friend roasts someone who isn't there. It's mean, and it's getting laughs.

options.t: Laugh along. Say something privately later.
Stay quiet and let it scroll by.
DM them: "okay, that was harsh."
Say it in the chat: "not cool."

cards.prompt: Two people share costs. One earns twice as much. Fair is...

options.t: Totally A
Leaning A
Both / depends
Leaning B
Totally B

cards.prompt: You're exhausted and a friend needs you. A good friend...

options.t: Totally A
Leaning A
Both / depends
Leaning B
Totally B

cards.b: says so and picks another night.

cards.prompt: Real friends...

options.t: Totally A
Leaning A
Both / depends
Leaning B
Totally B

cards.prompt: First hangout. They invited you. The bill lands.

options.t: Totally A
Leaning A
Both / depends
Leaning B
Totally B

cards.prompt: Five years from now, you'd rather hear...

options.t: Totally A
Leaning A
Both / depends
Leaning B
Totally B

cards.b: "Your life looks exactly how you wanted."

cards.prompt: Think of the last time a friend needed you on a night you were running on empty. What did you do?

options.t: Showed up and stayed till 2am.
Gave them an hour, then said goodnight.
Replied the next morning. Felt bad.
Said "can't tonight, tomorrow?"

cards.prompt: After that night, what stuck with you most?

options.t: Glad I was there.
Tired, but worth it.
A little resentful, honestly.
Guilty I wasn't there more.
Relieved I kept my sleep.

cards.prompt: Think of the last time a message that mattered showed "Read" and no reply.

options.t: Forgot about it. They'd answer eventually.
Noticed, then got on with my day.
Kept checking if they'd been online since.
Reread my message like it was evidence.

cards.prompt: When nothing came back, what showed up first?

options.t: Nothing. I got busy.
A small sting.
Worry. Are they okay?
Annoyed. I would've replied.
Relief. One less conversation.

cards.prompt: Your last free day with nothing planned. How much of it went to your closest person?

options.t: Nearly all of it. Even the grocery run.
The afternoon together, then solo.
A few memes. The rest was mine.
Kept it for me. We caught up later.

cards.prompt: Think of the last bill you split with friends. How did it go?

options.t: Split it evenly. Easy.
Split evenly. I'd only ordered a salad.
Whoever was doing better paid more.
Covered it myself. Never brought it up.

cards.prompt: The last surprise money you got: a refund, birthday cash, a bonus. Where did it go?

options.t: Gone within a week, on something fun.
Some fun, the rest saved.
Saved most. One small treat.
Savings or bills. Barely noticed.

cards.prompt: The last new thing you really wanted to try. How did you start?

options.t: Tested it on weekends. Changed nothing else.
Started small, went bigger once it worked.
Jumped in. Googled everything along the way.
Still planning it. The notes app is full.

cards.prompt: The last friendship or group chat that went quiet on your side. What happened?

options.t: Said something, and we talked it out.
Dropped hints and hoped it sorted itself.
Let it fade. My replies got slower.
Muted it. Never looked back.

cards.prompt: The last time your family pushed back on a plan of yours. What happened next?

options.t: Changed the plan. Kept the peace.
Met them halfway.
Went ahead, and explained. A lot.
Did it. Told them after.

cards.prompt: And afterward, what did you mostly feel?

options.t: Relief.
Guilt.
Annoyed.
Proud of myself.
Nothing much.

cards.prompt: The last time a friend asked what you honestly thought of something they made.

options.t: Told them the truth in the first sentence.
One nice thing, then the truth.
Mostly compliments. The truth got one line.
"I love it!" and changed the subject.

cards.prompt: The last time someone offered you more responsibility. What did you do?

options.t: Took it before they finished asking.
Took it and traded something off my plate.
Asked for time, then said no.
Said no right away. I like my life this size.

cards.prompt: You have six months of savings and an idea you can't stop thinking about.

options.t: Keep the job. Build it on weekends.
Start small. Quit only if it takes off.
Take a long leave and go for it.
Quit Friday. Figure it out as I go.

cards.prompt: Your boss offers you the lead on a big project. More credit, more hours, your evenings gone.

options.t: Yes before they finish the sentence.
Yes, if something else comes off my plate.
Ask for a day, then probably say no.
"Thanks, but I like my evenings."

cards.prompt: A group chat you used to love has gone weird. Nobody's fighting. It just feels off.

options.t: Say it: "hey, are we okay?"
Drop a meme and see who bites.
Reply slower and slower.
Mute it. Life moves on.

cards.prompt: A friend asks to borrow $300. "I'll pay you back soon." Soon is doing a lot of work.

options.t: Send it. Never mention it again.
Send it with a vague "no rush."
Send it with "by the 15th?"
"Not this time, sorry."

cards.prompt: You get a great job offer in another city. Your family says it's a mistake. Nothing actually keeps you home.

options.t: Turn it down. Not worth the fallout.
Ask for six months to bring them around.
Take it, after a week of explaining why.
Sign the offer. Tell them after.

cards.prompt: Your friend's birthday plan: a weekend away, $600 each. That's your fun budget for two months.

options.t: Book it. Noodles till spring.
Go, and quietly skip the pricey dinner.
Sit it out. Plan their birthday dinner later.
Say my budget and pitch a cheaper version.

cards.prompt: Your closest person suggests you both share phone passcodes. Just an idea.

options.t: Sure. Here's mine right now.
Fine, for emergencies.
Hmm. Can I think about it?
I'd rather not. Ask me anything instead.

cards.prompt: Someone offers you a free year living in a city you've never been to. Your life here is good.

options.t: Packing tonight.
Go, after a very long spreadsheet.
Tempting. I'll visit for a week instead.
Pass. My people are here.

cards.prompt: Your closest person got close to someone else. Nothing physical, but the late-night talks that were yours are now theirs. What hurts more?

options.t: The talks. Those were ours.
Mostly the talks. A bit the hiding.
Mostly the hiding. A bit the talks.
The hiding. We never agreed to secrets.

cards.prompt: A friend sends you a long apology. It is very obviously written by ChatGPT.

options.t: Accept it. They cared enough to try.
Accept it, then tease them about it.
Reply: "got it. Now in your words?"
Leave it on read until they call.

cards.prompt: A friend asks you to help carry a couch up four flights. It's your only day off.

options.t: "Yes. I'm bringing snacks."
"I can do the first two hours."
"Take my car and my moral support."
"Can't, but I'm sending pizza."

cards.prompt: The group trip house is $1,200. One room is way bigger than the rest. What do you pitch?

options.t: Split it evenly. Keep it simple.
Even split, and the big room buys dinner.
Big room pays a little more.
Price every room by size.

cards.prompt: Your closest person wants to spend all of Sunday together. You'd planned a solo day.

options.t: Cancel my plan. Sunday's theirs.
Half the day together, half mine.
Keep my plan. Offer them the evening.
Keep my plan. Another Sunday.

cards.prompt: Your favorite artist adds a surprise show this week. Tickets are $180.

options.t: Bought before finishing the announcement.
Bought, after checking my budget twice.
Waiting for resale prices.
Next tour. Probably.

cards.prompt: A friend shows you a haircut they got an hour ago. It is not great.

options.t: "Honestly? Not your best. Here's a fix."
"The color's great. The cut needs a week."
"It'll grow on me!"
"Obsessed."

cards.prompt: You're offered the lead on a group project. More credit, more work, and it overlaps a trip.

options.t: Take the lead. Move the trip.
Take it and shorten the trip.
Take a smaller role.
Pass. I'm going on the trip.

cards.prompt: A friend has canceled plans with you three times this month.

options.t: "Hey, is something up with us?"
Invite them once more and see.
Wait for them to reach out.
Stop inviting them. No hard feelings.
